title: MBEC Versus MBIC: the Lack of Differentiation in Biofilm Methodology
author: Thieme, Hartung, et al.

steps.title: Prepare bacterial suspensions
steps.instruction: Adjust three clinical isolates of each species (Enterococcus faecium, Enterococcus faecalis, Staphylococcus aureus, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Klebsiella pneumoniae) to a 0.5 McFarland density in the appropriate broth: Müller‑Hinton broth for enterococci and Todd‑Hewitt broth for the other species (both from Karl Roth, Karlsruhe, Germany).

steps.title: Inoculate microtiter plates
steps.instruction: Dispense the prepared suspensions into plastic microtiter plates (Greiner Bio‑one, Frickenhausen, Germany) in triplicate wells for each isolate.

steps.title: Incubate for biofilm formation
steps.instruction: Incubate the plates at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂, without shaking for 48 h to allow mature biofilm development.

steps.title: Refresh medium (mock treatment)
steps.instruction: After 48 h, carefully remove the spent medium and add fresh appropriate broth to each well (no antimicrobial added) to mimic a mock antimicrobial exposure, then continue incubation for an additional 24 h (total 72 h).

steps.title: Harvest biofilms at each time point
steps.instruction: At both the 48 h and 72 h time points, wash each well gently with sterile PBS, then resuspend the biofilm cells in a known volume of sterile buffer.

steps.title: Serially dilute and plate
steps.instruction: Prepare a series of 10‑fold dilutions of each resuspended biofilm sample, plate appropriate dilutions on agar plates, and incubate under suitable conditions for colony formation.

steps.title: Count colonies and calculate CFU/mL
steps.instruction: After incubation, count colonies on plates that contain 30–300 colonies, multiply by the dilution factor and the inverse of the resuspension volume to obtain CFU per millilitre for each biofilm sample.
